security_audit.summary: The static Ruby backtick findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline formatting. No prompt injection language was found in SKILL.md. The meaningful risks are the broad belt CLI permission, remote image service calls, and optional related skill installation examples.

remediation.suggestion: Limit allowed commands to the specific belt app actions needed for image generation, and require confirmation before each remote request.

remediation.issue: External prompt and image data transfer
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before sending prompts, source image URLs, or private images to inference.sh or downstream model providers.
Label npx skills add commands as optional manual steps, and avoid assistant-run installation without explicit user consent.

content.user_title: Generate AI Images with inference.sh Models
content.value_statement: Teams need quick access to many image models without memorizing each CLI command. This skill provides ready prompts for generation, editing, upscaling, and image stitching.
actual_capabilities: Shows belt CLI commands for image generation through inference.sh apps.
Lists supported image models and their common use cases.
Provides examples for text-to-image, image editing, upscaling, and stitching.
Uses source image URLs for edit, upscale, and multi-image workflows.
Points users to inference.sh documentation for running apps and image examples.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and an authenticated account.
Sends prompts, source images, and options to external inference services.
Model availability, pricing, output quality, and parameters can change.
Does not provide legal, copyright, or brand safety review for generated images.

use_cases.title: Create Campaign Visuals
use_cases.description: Generate draft images for ads, social posts, and landing pages using model-specific prompts.

use_cases.title: Explore Product Concepts
use_cases.description: Produce product mockups, style variations, and edited source images for early design review.

use_cases.title: Prototype Image Workflows
use_cases.description: Test generation, upscaling, and stitching commands before adding image steps to an app workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner Image Prompt
prompt_templates.scenario: You want one image from a simple idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate an image of [subject] in [style]. Use a model that fits speed and quality. Ask before running the CLI command.

prompt_templates.title: Product Mockup Prompt
prompt_templates.scenario: You need a commercial visual with clear details.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a product image for [product] with [lighting], [background], and [aspect ratio]. Recommend the model and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Image Editing Prompt
prompt_templates.scenario: You have a source image that needs changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit this image URL: [image URL]. Change [specific element] while preserving [important details]. Confirm the URL is safe to send.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Workflow Prompt
prompt_templates.scenario: You need a multi-step image pipeline.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a workflow to generate [concept], upscale the best result, and stitch it with [second image]. Include model choices and approval steps.

output_examples.input: Generate a studio product image for a ceramic coffee mug.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a suitable image model, refines the visual prompt, and asks before running the belt command.

output_examples.input: Change the background of my uploaded product photo to a beach scene.
output_examples.output: The skill prepares an image editing request, notes that the source image URL will be sent externally, and requests confirmation.

output_examples.input: Upscale an image and combine it with another reference image.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines an upscale step and a stitching step, with separate confirmations for each remote service call.

best_practices: Review prompts and source image URLs before any belt command runs.
Start with low-cost models for exploration, then use higher-quality models for final assets.
Keep generated assets labeled with the model, prompt, date, and usage rights review status.
anti_patterns: Do not send confidential images or unreleased product designs without approval.
Do not assume every model supports the same options or image sizes.
Do not install related skills or run extra commands without explicit user consent.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps run inference.sh image apps for generation, editing, upscaling, and image stitching.

faq.question: Does it require an external account?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples require the inference.sh belt CLI and a logged-in account.

faq.question: Can it edit existing images?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes examples that send source image URLs to image editing models.

faq.question: Does it work in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Are images generated locally?
faq.answer: No. The workflow uses the belt CLI to request images from external inference services.

faq.question: What should users review before running it?
faq.answer: Users should review prompts, image URLs, model choice, expected cost, and data sharing rules.
